content: I'll read the test image to analyze the visual symptoms.

**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part affected:** Wheat head/spike (florets/spikelets)
- **Key features:**
  - Several spikelets show **bleached/tan-orange discoloration** — the glumes have turned a pale orange-brown color
  - The affected spikelets appear **shriveled and discolored**, with a characteristic salmon/orange-tan hue
  - The disease appears to affect individual spikelets while adjacent ones remain green
  - The glumes are spreading/gaping open
  - No visible fungal sporulation masses (ruling out smuts/rusts which would show spore pustules)
  - The bleached, water-soaked to tan-orange appearance is localized to individual spikelets

**Reasoning:**

This pattern — bleached/orange-tan spikelets on a wheat head, with the characteristic "tombstone" or premature bleaching of individual florets — is classic **Head Scab** (Fusarium Head Blight). The salmon/orange discoloration of the glumes and the localized blighting of spikelets partway up the spike are hallmark symptoms. Stripe Rust would show yellow pustule stripes on leaves/glumes. Loose Smut would replace the entire head with dark spore masses. The orange-tan bleached glumes spreading from infection points is highly characteristic of Fusarium head scab.
